evals.prompt: The vault contains one file named Alpha.md at Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md. It is referenced by [[Alpha]] in two other files. User says: 'Rename Alpha to Beta.'
evals.expected_output: Agent globs the vault for Alpha with its own glob tool, resolving it to the single path Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md, since the command takes a vault-relative path rather than a bare name. Agent composes the destination as the FULL path 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Beta.md', joining the source's folder to the new basename and appending the .md itself. It must NOT pass a bare 'Beta.md', which would move the file to the vault root. Agent does not ask the user to supply an extension or a folder. Agent runs `vault move --path Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md --destination Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Beta.md --output json` with no --apply to preview, gets back a complete report (applied: false, repaired_links with 2 entries across 2 distinct paths) with nothing mutated, and presents that itemized preview with the rename for confirmation. After the user confirms, agent re-runs the same command with --apply added. Agent confirms applied: true in the return before reporting success: 2 references rewritten across 2 files.

evals.prompt: The vault contains two files both named Alpha.md: one at Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md and one at Projects/Personal/SideProject/Inbox/Alpha.md. User says: 'Rename Alpha to Beta.'
evals.expected_output: Agent globs for Alpha and gets two matches. Because `vault move` needs an unambiguous --path and does no name resolution itself, the agent resolves the ambiguity up front, using AskUserQuestion with the two matching paths as options rather than guessing. After the user selects one, agent composes --destination as that same folder plus 'Beta.md', previews without --apply, confirms, then re-runs with --apply.

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Long-Verbose-Plan-Name.md. User says: 'Rename Long-Verbose-Plan-Name to Short-Name' (no .md extension on either name).
evals.expected_output: Agent globs to resolve the source, then calls `vault move` with --path 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Long-Verbose-Plan-Name.md' and --destination 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Short-Name.md'. The agent supplies both the folder and the .md, because a bare 'Short-Name' is refused with invalid_path and a bare 'Short-Name.md' would relocate the doc to the vault root rather than rename it in place. The agent does not surface any of this to the user, who asked for 'Short-Name' in the same folder and gets exactly that.

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md. User says: 'Move Alpha to Projects/Personal/SideProject/Inbox/Alpha.md' (full destination path given, same basename, and that folder already exists).
evals.expected_output: Agent resolves --path to Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md and passes --destination as the full path given, with the extension already present so nothing is appended. Because the basename is unchanged, no bare-link rewrite is needed, but the path-qualified scan still runs and any [[Vault/Alpha]]-style link is repaired. Agent previews without --apply and confirms before the applying call. The agent does NOT claim the command will create the destination folder, since it creates no folders and this case works only because the folder already exists.

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Gamma.md and a separate, already-existing Resources/Software/Beta.md. A bystander bare link [[Beta]] lives in a file close to Resources/Software/, currently resolving to Resources/Software/Beta.md. User says: 'Rename Gamma in the Vault Inbox folder to Beta', i.e. rename it into the occupied 'Beta' basename, moving it close enough to the bystander's linking file that it would win the resolution if left bare.
evals.expected_output: Agent resolves --path to Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Gamma.md, composes --destination as 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Beta.md', previews, confirms, then re-runs with --apply. There is no --force parameter and the agent does not attempt to pass one. Entering the occupied 'Beta' basename still succeeds. The command emits any link to the moved file as full-path, since 'Beta' is no longer unique, and because the rename would have flipped the bystander [[Beta]] link's resolution toward the newly-renamed file, it pins that bystander link to its current target's full path (Resources/Software/Beta.md) rather than leaving it to silently re-resolve. That pinning appears in pinned_links[] as {path, line, from, to} entries, and the preview already showed it before the user confirmed. Agent reports repaired_links as usual AND reports the pinned_links entries, e.g. '1 bystander link was pinned to its full path to preserve its target.' Agent does not mention force, ambiguous_references, or basename_collision, none of which exist in the current contract.

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md with no other files referencing it. User says: 'Rename Alpha.md to Nonexistent-Folder/Beta.md' where Nonexistent-Folder does not yet exist.
evals.expected_output: Agent passes --destination 'Nonexistent-Folder/Beta.md' and the call is REFUSED with parent_missing, whose data.parent names 'Nonexistent-Folder'. A move brings no folder into existence. The agent recognizes this rather than reporting a failed rename, and either creates the folder with `vault create --path Nonexistent-Folder --kind folder` and retries the move, or asks the user first if creating a new top-level vault folder is a decision they should make. The agent must NOT claim the destination parent is created automatically, and must NOT fall back to New-Item, mkdir, or a filesystem workaround for either step.

evals.prompt: User says: 'Rename Doesnt-Exist to Something-Else.' No file named Doesnt-Exist.md exists anywhere in the vault.
evals.expected_output: Agent globs the vault for Doesnt-Exist and finds no match. Because `vault move` requires an existing, resolved --path, the agent catches the miss at resolution time, telling the user no such file exists and stopping, rather than running the command or attempting a workaround such as Move-Item or manual git commands. Running the command would refuse with path_not_found, but resolving first is the expected behavior.

evals.prompt: vault-doc-archive calls vault-doc-rename programmatically with fully-resolved OldPath 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Plan-Alpha.md' and NewPath 'Areas/Personal/Vault/Archive/Plan-Alpha-2026-06-20.md'.
evals.expected_output: Agent skips confirmation AND the preview call entirely, because the programmatic entry point means the calling skill already resolved and confirmed the operation, and skips source globbing since OldPath is already a resolved path. NewPath is already a full vault-relative path carrying .md, so nothing is composed or appended. Agent makes exactly one `vault move` invocation, with --apply and --output json, without asking the user. Agent returns the command's summary (applied, moved[], repaired_links[], pinned_links[]) to the calling skill. It does not report namingWarnings, folderNoteOrphaned, pureMove, or lockWarning, none of which exist as fields.

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Notes.md. User says: 'Rename Notes.md to Notes.txt, I want it as a plain text file now.'
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes this as a file-type conversion rather than a rename. `vault move` requires the destination to be a markdown note and refuses .txt with invalid_path ('names no note - every operand here is a markdown note or a folder'), with no override parameter of any kind. The agent tells the user the move command cannot change what a file is and stops. It does NOT silently send 'Notes.md', does NOT try to pass a force, override, or allow-conversion argument, and does NOT fall back to Move-Item, git mv, or any filesystem workaround. Offering to do the conversion by other means is acceptable only as a suggestion the user must approve; performing it is not.

evals.prompt: The vault contains Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Alpha.md referenced from several notes. User says: 'Rename Alpha to Beta, but show me exactly which files will change first.'
evals.expected_output: Agent resolves the source by glob, then runs `vault move` WITHOUT --apply. The command runs plan and validate and returns the complete report (applied: false, moved[], repaired_links[], pinned_links[]) with nothing mutated. Agent lists the affected files to the user from repaired_links[], counting distinct path values for the file count and total array entries for the occurrence count, since two links on the same line are two entries sharing a path and line and must not be deduped away. The agent does NOT tell the user that a preview is unavailable or that the command has no dry-run mode, because omitting --apply is exactly that preview. After the user confirms, the agent re-runs the identical command with --apply appended.

evals.prompt: The agent has just run `vault move` without --apply to preview renaming Alpha to Beta. The command printed {"applied": false, "path": "Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Beta.md", "content_hash": "...", "case_only": false, "moved": ["Areas/Personal/Vault/Inbox/Beta.md"], "repaired_links": [3 entries across 3 paths], "pinned_links": [], "asserted_authority": []}.
evals.expected_output: Agent treats this as a plan rather than a result, reporting to the user what WILL change (3 references across 3 files) and asking for confirmation. It must not say the rename is done, must not report '3 references rewritten' in the past tense, and must not skip the applying call. The applied field is the discriminator, and applied: false means nothing happened. An empty pinned_links[] is the normal case and warrants no comment to the user, and asserted_authority is operational detail that is never surfaced.

evals.prompt: The agent runs `vault move` to rename a doc and the command exits non-zero, printing {"code": "dependency_unavailable", "message": "The search engine could not be started, so no search or enumeration can run until the deployment is corrected."}.
evals.expected_output: Agent reports the refusal verbatim and stops. It states plainly that NOTHING was moved and no links were rewritten, and that this is a deployment fault (ripgrep is unreachable) rather than a vault or content problem. The agent must NOT retry in a loop, must NOT report the rename as partially applied, and must NOT fall back to moving the file by other means such as Move-Item, git mv, or Edit, because a move without the reference scan would leave every wikilink pointing at the old name. Explaining that the vault deployment needs fixing, or offering to diagnose it, is the appropriate next step.

evals.prompt: User says: 'Rename the gizmo doc to "gizmo reference notes".' The source resolves to Resources/Gizmo-Reference.md.
evals.expected_output: The requested basename is outside the vault's name grammar, having a lower-case start and spaces. The agent normalizes it when composing the destination, to 'Resources/Gizmo-Reference-Notes.md', rather than passing the user's raw wording through. If it does pass a non-conforming name, the command REFUSES with invalid_name and data.suggested carries an accepted spelling; the agent then retries with the suggestion, confirming with the user first if the suggested spelling changes the meaning. The key behavior is that the agent treats invalid_name as a refusal where nothing moved, rather than as a warning attached to a successful move.
